newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn politicians set to urge watch on Scientology.
newsitem.headline: Bonn politicians set to urge watch on Scientology.

text.p: A parliamentary commission is likely to recommend that Germany's anti-extremist watchdog puts the Church of Scientology under observation, a commission member said on Sunday.
Ronald Pofalla told Welt am Sonntag newspaper that Scientology, based on the teachings of late American science fiction writer L. Ron Hubbard, bound its members in a "slave-like system".
"I am sure that the Bundestag (lower house) commission... will recommend that the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution observes Scientologists," he said.

Pofalla said he had prepared a paper on the "concrete dangers of the Church of Scientology" for the commission into "so-called sects and psycho-groups", which is due to present its findings to parliament on June 26.
Pofalla, a member of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats, said the church was dangerous for the health and the finances of its members.

Germany sees the church as a profit-making organisation rather than a religion. The southern states of Baden-Wuerttemberg and Bavaria already have Scientology observed by their anti-extremist watchdogs.
Scientologists have accused Germany of mounting a "hysterical witchhunt" against it at taxpayers' expense.

This year's annual human rights report from the U.S. State Department listed Scientology's allegations of persecution in Germany, and the issue has prompted protests from U.S. entertainment celebrities.
